newsitem.title: USA: Healthy Mexican economy in U.S. interest - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Healthy Mexican economy in U.S. interest - Rubin.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Thursday that it was in the U.S. interest that the Mexican economy be healthy and that Washington support President Ernesto Zedillo's reform effort.

Rubin told a House Appropriations subcommittee that at the time of the 1994 Mexican peso crisis and the subsequent U.S. financial aid package in 1995, the administration believed it was in U.S. interests to have a healthy Mexican economy.

He called Zedillo's economic program "courageous" and said the best thing Washington could do to help improve Mexico's economic and political stability was to support a "courageious and honest" president.

Rubin told the panel that Mexico still faces enormous social, political and economic problems as well as problems of corruption and drugs. He said the administration made the right decision in certifying Mexico as an ally in the war against drugs.
